title: 3-Year Treasury Note auction (November refunding new issue) — leg one of three, pulled to Monday by the Veterans Day closure
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) and its text layer decompressed stream-by-stream. Row reads verbatim `3-Year NOTE / Wednesday, November 04, 2026 / Monday, November 09, 2026 / Monday, November 16, 2026` — no trailing `R`, so a NEW ISSUE, announced by the 2026-11-04 quarterly refunding statement. 1:00pm ET is Treasury's standing coupon-auction convention and is NOT separately sourced. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-30y-bond-2026-11-12 never-assessed initial research (2026-09-08), sweeping that event's +/-5-day corridor. THIS PROPOSAL KNOWINGLY REVISITS A PRIOR DECLINE, and says so rather than filing silently: the treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-11-12 lane saw this row in the same PDF on the same day and deliberately did not file it, reasoning that the 3Y and 10Y legs 'are sized and announced by treasury-refunding-2026-11-04, their natural owner, and filing a block of five auctions off one sweep would be noise rather than information.' That reasoning is sound about SIZING and does not settle TRACKING, and the calendar itself is the evidence: it already carries treasury-3y-note-2026-09-08 and treasury-3y-note-2026-10-06 as first-class medium-impact entries under the same refunding owner. November's leg being absent is an inconsistency in the series, not a spared duplicate — and only one auction is filed here, not five. EXPECTED SIZE, per the grid rather than any current document: $58B. Every 3-Year new issue has printed $58B for 21 consecutive months since 2025-01-06 (fiscaldata auctions_query, pulled 2026-09-08, zero deviations), and no nominal coupon size has moved anywhere since April 2024; the number becomes published on 2026-11-04. STRUCTURAL NOTE: this leg sits on MONDAY, one day earlier than a normal refunding block's Tuesday, because the bond market is closed Wednesday 2026-11-11 for Veterans Day. That is Treasury's standing response, not an improvisation — in all three prior years where Veterans Day fell on a Wednesday (2009, 2015, 2020) the 3-Year sold on Monday November 9, 3 for 3. Proposed as an estimate; symbols: [] and no house playbook is rates-keyed, so nothing here licenses an entry.
